items.title: First for RNA therapy: man with rare motor-neuron disease improves after treatment
items.summary: Gene-targeting treatments could be used to treat other people with rare forms of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

items.title: AI cracked the Navier–Stokes challenge. What does that mean for physics?
items.summary: Physicists and mathematicians are going beyond the classic equations of fluid dynamics to understand turbulence — often with the help of AI.

items.title: How a team of AIs discovered a promising lung-cancer drug
items.summary: Researchers developed a ‘virtual biotech’ made up of as many as 37,000 agents reporting to a ‘chief scientist’.

items.title: Overmassive black holes and little red dots naturally form in simulations
items.summary: Observations from the JWST reveal an unexpectedly abundant population of little red dots and overmassive black holes in the early Universe, which are confirmed by their formation in fully cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations.

items.title: Targeted genomic integration and rearrangement using prime assembly
items.summary: Prime assembly enables RNA-guided integration of medium-to-large DNA sequences in human cells without requiring double-strand breaks or cell cycle progression, and supports exon recoding, transgene insertion and megabase-scale rearrangements.

items.title: Transplanted human brain-tissue takes root in mice without a cortex
items.summary: Extensive cellular integration might provide platform for in vivo testing of new therapies — plus, the AI tool that turns papers into ‘virtual corresponding authors’.

items.title: AI co-scientists are revolutionizing how research is done
items.summary: Artificial-intelligence systems can generate hypotheses, design experiments and analyse data — but humans still need to decide what makes sense.

items.title: How to make a brain: new experiments challenge existing picture
items.summary: Research also uncovers an efficient way to grow hindbrain cells from stem cells — a difficult feat.

items.title: Take a risk or play it safe? Neuronal tug-of-war helps the brain decide
items.summary: Using a video game involving bombs and treasure chests, researchers show how neural activity flickers between two regions of the frontal cortex when the brain weighs up a tricky decision.

items.title: Developmental xenocortication using human-derived organoids in mice
items.summary: Xenocortication with human neurons enables circuit- and behaviour-level analysis of neurodevelopment in mice.

items.title: Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents
items.summary: Paper2Agent converts research papers into interactive artificial intelligence agents by turning manuscripts, code and data into model context protocol-based tool-invoking systems that reproduce original results, answer new scientific queries and collaborate to generate novel insights.

items.title: Continuous-wave laser absorption spectroscopy of the thorium-229 nucleus
items.summary: Absorption spectroscopy of thorium-229 nuclear excited states in a thorium-doped calcium fluoride crystal demonstrates a path towards a much more efficient way to build a highly stable and robust solid-state optical nuclear clock.

items.title: Topographic structure and function of locus coeruleus noradrenaline neurons
items.summary: Dorsal and ventral noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus form topographic subpopulations whose projection patterns and activity encode choice switching, reward-prediction errors and disregard of reward-predictive cues, supporting flexible learning behaviour.

items.title: Road transport of trapped antiprotons
items.summary: Researchers demonstrate successful road transport of trapped antiprotons, establishing a practical method for moving antimatter to quieter laboratories and substantially improving future tests of matter–antimatter symmetry.

items.title: Scalable near-real-time Bayesian phylogenetics for outbreaks with Delphy
items.summary: Delphy makes near-real-time and scalable Bayesian phylogenetics possible for growing viral outbreaks, enabling public health bodies anywhere to analyse and react to their own data with state-of-the-art accuracy and minimal friction.

items.title: Identification of broadly tumour-reactive γδ TCRs from multiple myeloma
items.summary: A machine-learning algorithm, PreGame, is developed to identify tumour-reactive γδ T cells from single-cell CITE sequencing data, and expansion of this cell population can be used as a biomarker of therapeutic response.

items.title: A retinoic acid autoregulatory loop governing prefrontal–motor arealization
items.summary: MEIS2, encoding a transcription factor linked to intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, is a key hub of a retinoic-acid-associated gene regulatory network.

items.title: Molecular-level observation of the self-assembly of a virus-like particle
items.summary: Using mass photometry combined with a single-molecule trapping method allows real-time monitoring of the assembly of individual virus-like particles with molecular resolution, enabling observation and quantification of their self-assembly pathways and dynamics.

items.title: Electrically controllable superconducting memory effect in UTe<sub>2</sub>
items.summary: Observations of a memory effect in the p-wave superconductor candidate UTe2, which can be controlled by varying the strength and duration of the electrically applied stimuli, are described.

items.title: Cohesin reshapes replication fork contacts to aid fork slowing and reversal
items.summary: Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion limits sister-fork coupling and tethers nearby replication forks under replication stress, promoting fork reversal and slowing fork progression to safeguard genome stability.

items.title: Cognitive resilience helps to predict Alzheimer’s dementia
items.summary: The trait could explain why symptoms vary in severity between people with similar brain pathology.

items.title: Inflection points and transitions in Alzheimer’s disease
items.summary: Inflection points and transitions in Alzheimer’s disease

items.title: Why most stars don’t have outbursts like the Sun’s
items.summary: A strong magnetic field can disrupt a star’s ability to produce the fountains of matter called coronal mass ejections.

items.title: Mitochondrial fission factor senses and governs ferroptosis
items.summary: The mitochondrial–peroxisomal fission adaptor MFF is identified as a selective pro-ferroptotic mediator, and the newly developed MFF–SPARK sensor enables high-content screening of ferroptosis-sensitizing compounds and the discovery of upstream regulators of MFF.

items.title: Electroluminescent photoresists extending lithographic scaling to OLEDs
items.summary: Electroluminescent photoresists synthesized via atom transfer radical polymerization can be directly patterned by ultraviolet and electron-beam lithography, and used to fabricate monolithic, multicolour organic-light-emitting-diode micro-pixel arrays.

items.title: Evolution and heterogeneity of lethal metastatic bladder cancer subtypes
items.summary: A rapid autopsy programme provides valuable resources to enable detailed molecular and genetic analyses of the temporal evolution of aggressive histological subtypes and therapy resistance in metastatic bladder cancer.

items.title: Rapid patient-specific neural networks for X-ray to volume registration
items.summary: xvr makes pan-anatomical 2D/3D rigid registration accessible to broad clinical and research communities.

items.title: Heterogeneous photonic integration of single-crystalline nanomembranes
items.summary: A framework consisting of advanced epitaxy and layer lift-off techniques uses heterogeneous photonic integration of single-crystalline nanomembranes to infuse desired functionalities into silicon and silicon nitride photonics, demonstrating ultraefficient electro-optical and magneto-optical modulation.

items.title: Sex without crossovers mimics clonal reproduction in Rhynchospora tenuis
items.summary: Rhynchospora tenuis undergoes obligate, genome-wide achiasmy in both male and female meiosis.

items.title: Mutational constraints on RSV F and its neutralization by antibodies
items.summary: How respiratory syncytial virus mutations affect antibody neutralization is defined, and a biophysical model of the mechanism is provided, to show how Fab potency and epitope specificity combine to determine the effects of viral mutations on antibody neutralization.

items.title: Daily briefing: How to turn a paper into an AI agent
items.summary: A new tool is designed to help researchers interact with published papers. Plus, promising news for an RNA-based treatment for ALS and how psychoactive drugs might have shaped pre-Incan culture.

items.title: Mercury is shrinking with age — faster than thought
items.summary: Impacts by space objects have obscured some of the evidence of the planet’s contraction over the past 4.5 billion years.

items.title: How fast are you ageing? Ask AI
items.summary: A new system will help scientists to refine large language models for longevity research and clarify ‘biological’ age.

items.title: Who gets credit in the AI era? OpenAI maths bombshell sparks debate
items.summary: Controversy around OpenAI’s claim to have solved the Navier–Stokes problem highlights how researchers could be inadvertently sharing — and absorbing— ideas through chatbots.

items.title: Mechanisms of Transcriptional Regulation by Salicylic Acid Receptors
items.summary: Mechanisms of Transcriptional Regulation by Salicylic Acid Receptors

items.title: Transcriptional activation of plant immunity by salicylic acid
items.summary: A mechanistic basis for how the hormone salicylic acid promotes transcriptional activation during plant immune responses is described.

items.title: Assessing biological degradation of non-hydrolysable synthetic polymers
items.summary: The evidence for biological degradation of non-hydrolysable synthetic polymers is critically evaluated to propose best-practice principles for experimental design that should promote reproducibility and impact across this field.

items.title: Losing your way of life to climate change matters — and we need a way to measure it
items.summary: Climate losses extend beyond property and income. Policymakers need ways to assess what people value, experience and ultimately stand to lose.

items.title: Europe pushes for space independence amid geopolitical rifts
items.summary: The European Union is easing its reliance on US space infrastructure — and is seeking to grow its satellite and launch operations.

items.title: Schoolhouse meals serve up an income bump
items.summary: Modelling shows a link between feeding programmes and higher potential earning in five African nations.

items.title: Exclusive: New evidence for hidden chambers beyond Tutankhamun’s tomb
items.summary: Geophysical survey yields ‘tantalizing’ data that could point to Nefertiti’s burial place — but it’s too early to draw definitive conclusions.

items.title: Development of a random background to understand ligand optimization
items.summary: An approach to improve efficiency and establish a background expectation for ligand potency optimization is described.

items.title: Briefing Chat: Evidence mounts for hidden chambers beyond Tutankhamun's tomb
items.summary: Nature staff discuss data that could point to Nefertiti’s burial place — plus, the implant that translates brain activity into speech and gestures.

items.title: Chinese companies doubled down on science after US tech restrictions
items.summary: Affected Chinese companies adjusted their sources of knowledge to stay competitive.

items.title: Daily briefing: Fresh evidence for hidden chambers at Tutankhamun’s tomb
items.summary: Scans support the idea that as-yet-unexplored chambers might hold the remains of the Egyptian queen Nefertiti. Plus, mathematical controversy and beautiful ctenophores.

items.title: Six principles for supporting academic freedom in universities
items.summary: Many academics are concerned about threats to independent enquiry in higher education. Here’s how it can be protected while taking legitimate concerns into account.

items.title: How research funding took me out of the lab and into leadership
items.summary: Landing two large grants caused Anna Sandak to take on a managerial role in her team and made her reflect on what it means to contribute to research.

items.title: How do I change labs gracefully during my PhD?
items.summary: A scientist in training seeks help in finding a new adviser without damaging existing working relationships.

items.title: Author Correction: Genomic deletion of malic enzyme 2 confers collateral lethality in pancreatic cancer
items.summary: Author Correction: Genomic deletion of malic enzyme 2 confers collateral lethality in pancreatic cancer

authors: Francisco de Assis Guedes de Vasconcelos
